markscheme: M1: correct working with negatives, e.g. $-8 + 15 = 7$
questions.modelAnswer: Work from left to right: $-8 + 15 = 7$ (the numbers have different signs, so subtract $8$ from $15$ and keep the sign of the larger). Then $7 - 12 = -5$. Answer: $-5$.

questions.stem: Consider the numbers $12$ and $18$. (a) Find their highest common factor (HCF). (b) Find their lowest common multiple (LCM). (c) Are $12$ and $18$ coprime? Give a reason.
markscheme: B1: not coprime, because they share a factor greater than $1$ (HCF is $6$)
questions.modelAnswer: Factors of $12$: $1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12$. Factors of $18$: $1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18$. The largest factor they share is $6$, so HCF $= 6$. Multiples of $12$: $12, 24, 36, \ldots$ Multiples of $18$: $18, 36, \ldots$ The smallest multiple they share is $36$, so LCM $= 36$. Two numbers are coprime only when their HCF is $1$; since the HCF is $6$, $12$ and $18$ are not coprime.

markscheme: M1: $36 \times 4 = 144$ with the decimal point placed correctly
questions.modelAnswer: (a) Ignore the decimals first: $36 \times 4 = 144$. There are two decimal places in total (one in each number), so the answer is $1.44$. (b) Multiply both numbers by $10$ to make an easier division: $72 \div 9 = 8$. Answers: $1.44$ and $8$.

questions.stem: $a = 4$ and $b = -3$. Work out the value of $2a - b^2$.
questions.modelAnswer: Substitute the values: $2a - b^2 = 2(4) - (-3)^2 = 8 - 9 = -1$. Note that $(-3)^2 = 9$, since squaring a negative number gives a positive result. Answer: $-1$.

questions.stem: A bag contains $4$ red counters, $5$ blue counters and $1$ green counter. One counter is picked at random. Work out the probability that it is NOT blue.
markscheme: M1: $10$ counters in total and $5$ of them are not blue
questions.modelAnswer: There are $4 + 5 + 1 = 10$ counters in total. The counters that are not blue are the $4$ red and $1$ green, so $5$ favourable outcomes. Probability $= \dfrac{5}{10} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.stem: The mean of the five numbers $3, 7, 8, 12$ and $x$ is $7$. Work out the value of $x$.
markscheme: M1: total of the five numbers $= 5 \times 7 = 35$
questions.modelAnswer: If the mean of $5$ numbers is $7$, their total must be $5 \times 7 = 35$. The four known numbers add to $3 + 7 + 8 + 12 = 30$. So $x = 35 - 30 = 5$. Check: $30 + 5 = 35$ and $35 \div 5 = 7$ ✓
There are $1000$ m in $1$ km, so $2.4$ km $= 2.4 \times 1000 = 2400$ m. There are $100$ cm in $1$ m, so $2400$ m $= 2400 \times 100 = 240\,000$ cm. Answer: $240\,000$ cm.

questions.stem: Estimate the value of $\dfrac{58.3 \times 4.9}{2.1}$. Show clearly how you get your estimate.
markscheme: M1: rounds each number to $1$ significant figure: $60$, $5$ and $2$
questions.modelAnswer: Round each number to $1$ significant figure: $58.3 \approx 60$, $4.9 \approx 5$ and $2.1 \approx 2$. Then estimate $\dfrac{60 \times 5}{2} = \dfrac{300}{2} = 150$. The estimate is $150$ (the exact value is about $136$, so this is a sensible overestimate).
